video.title: Fantasy Basketball Shooting Guard Tier Rankings [NBA]

summary: Josh Lloyd ranks shooting guard eligible players in tiers for fantasy drafts, using Fantrax position eligibility, and gives his projected usage and minutes for many of them. Luka Doncic is alone in tier one, and Josh calls him a clear number three pick. Cade Cunningham and Anthony Edwards make up tier two, and Josh prefers Cade. He warns against single season myopia. He thinks Donovan Mitchell is not a first rounder, while Austin Reaves could finish ahead of him. He sees Jaylen Brown, Dyson Daniels and Norman Powell as undervalued. He sees Deni Avdija, Kon Knueppel, Kawhi Leonard and Dylan Harper as going too high. Throughout the show he leans on usage and minutes projections, the 240 minute rotation exercise, and doubts about 9-cat formula rankings.

rules.text: Positional tiers are fluid. Cutoffs shift between positions, so a player changing tiers from one position list to another should not be overread.
rules.quote: That's why some of these positional tier things I think can be

rules.text: Avoid single season myopia. Do not assume last season's result is what always happens. Look at a player's career range and at what changed around him.
rules.quote: single season myopia, where people just look back at what happened last season and that's it.

rules.text: Use past production as a base, then adjust for changed factors like new teammates and lost teammates.
rules.quote: I look at the production and and what did happen as a basis of what could happen, but factors need to be considered.

rules.text: Projected usage and minutes drive rankings. If you expect different usage or minutes, adjust the player's position yourself.
rules.quote: if you think that his usage will be higher or his minutes will be lower, then take that into consideration

rules.text: Injuries are largely unpredictable. A player seen as injury prone can stay healthy, and a durable player can get hurt.
rules.quote: players can stay healthy or players can get hurt. There's not a lot you can do about it.

rules.text: Leaning too hard on 9-cat formula rankings ('nine cat fluffery') can mislead player evaluation in both directions.
rules.quote: rooted in nine cap fluffery and that can lead to problems I think in evaluating players.

rules.text: Defensive stat differences are small in weekly terms. Going from 0.7 to 1 steal is about one extra steal per week, which is easy to flip.
rules.quote: going from 7 steals to one steal is one extra steal per week. It's so inconsequential.

rules.text: Good efficiency on low volume does not matter much.
rules.quote: good efficiency guy on lower volume is not that important.

rules.text: Be wary of players whose value came from teammates being absent. When those teammates return, their production drops.
rules.quote: really making hay while BS while BS have been out and then when they come back he disappears.

rules.text: The 240 game: every team game has 240 minutes to split among about 10 players. Use it to test whether a team's minutes projections are realistic.
rules.quote: 10-man rotation. Some play 11, maybe one team will play nine, but you've got to fit 240 minutes for 10 players.

rules.text: High usage rookies nearly always post bad percentages.
rules.quote: pretty bad percentages as nearly every high usage rookie does

rules.text: Expect second year players to take a jump forward.
rules.quote: we talked about secondyear players and big jumps jumps that they take forward.

rules.text: If you took injury risk or flyer picks earlier, balance them later with safe, steady players.
rules.quote: If you've taken flyer picks earlier, injury risk picks earlier, Wiggo is just solid here.

rules.text: Players at the bottom tier are deep league (14 team) picks or streamers who move on and off rosters.
rules.quote: you're picking them in 14 teamers and they're going to be on and off rosters of streamers throughout the year.

rules.text: Some players are much better in points leagues than in category leagues, so tiers differ by format.
rules.quote: you can see some differences who's better in category leagues who's better in points leagues
